target_customer: Frontier AI labs and AI application companies that buy expert-built training data, RL environments and benchmarks
problem: Models trained on outputs plateau; labs need expert reasoning data, rubrics and agent environments that general crowdwork cannot supply.
business_model: Project-based data and environment sales to AI labs
product_category: AI training data and RL environments

founders.name: Spencer Mateega
education: Wharton undergraduate, master's in computer science in progress
previous_startups: Earlier startup co-founded with Danny, sold
founders.background_notes: Forbes headline calls him a 23 year old; no birth year stated, so age not recorded.

founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder on the company About page per press; the YC page lists him only in a team section.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly operational excellence in recruiting experts and building QA pipelines, with some research in rubrics and environments; not research-grade model work.

defensibility.rationale: Lab relationships and expert networks help, but customer concentration and rivals such as Mercor, Surge and Scale make the position contestable per Sacra commentary.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established vendors compete rather than copy outright; Mercor and others now sell similar benchmarks and environments (2026 sources).

market_need_then: Frontier labs were spending heavily on expert data; Forbes and company statements report roughly 100 million dollars annualized revenue by April 2026, about 14 months after founding (company stated).

identity.visual_style: Research-lab styling per site copy; not detailed

branding.brand_signature: Tagline: We teach machines how experts think
branding.community_and_virality: Forbes coverage of the young founder and revenue run rate; Decrypt on a reported 3.2 billion dollar valuation; named collaborations with NVIDIA, Legora and Hebbia on its site.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press from Forbes and the rapid growth story, but the name itself is not explained and the buyer base is a small set of labs.

outcome_analysis: AfterQuery applied to YC with no product, then reportedly reached about 100 million dollars annualized revenue within roughly 14 months by selling expert training data to frontier labs. It closed a 30 million dollar Series A led by Altos in April 2026 and Forbes reported a later 3.2 billion dollar valuation round not yet closed. Risks are customer concentration and rivals Mercor, Surge and Scale.
notes: Series A confirmed by Business Wire release, SiliconANGLE and Pulse 2.0. Press says 'at a 300 million valuation' without stating pre or post, so post_money left null. A Seedtable entry shows a March 2025 pre-seed (aggregator only, unverified, not recorded). Forbes (per Decrypt) reported a 3.2 billion dollar valuation round that had not closed and had no named lead; not recorded as a round. Revenue figures are company stated or Sacra estimates. Dated competitor sources near January 2025 were not found; competitor pages found are from 2026 so the list is empty.
